title: Tate comparison computed by chosen Koszul augmentation lifts
statement: For every commutative ring A, ideal I and degree n, there is an A-linear map from the conormal exterior module [new-r4-conormal-exterior-module] to Tor_n^A(A/I,A/I) with the following property: for every finite tuple g in I and every projective resolution P of A/I there exists an augmentation-preserving Koszul chain map a into P. On every cycle representing a degree-n wedge after tensoring with A/I, the homology map of a equals the value of the comparison on the wedge of the conormal classes, transported by P.isoLeftDerivedObj. Only this chosen lift is asserted to satisfy the formula, rather than all augmentation lifts as in [new-r4-self-tor-conormal-predicate].

source.place: Tag 09PQ, Tate resolution computation of strictly commutative Tor; Tag 00LS, part (1), comparison lifting

proof.text: Use a free Tate dg algebra resolution of A/I to compute self-Tor, with its strictly graded commutative product. Identify degree-one classes with I/I² via the quotient boundary. Odd classes square to zero in all characteristics; their products are alternating and A/I-multilinear, yielding a map on the exterior conormal power.

Lift each tuple element to degree one of the Tate resolution and extend to a Koszul dg algebra map. Choose a comparison map from the free Tate complex to P preserving augmentation by inductive projective lifting. The composite gives the required chosen Koszul lift; its wedge products give the displayed formula under the canonical derived comparison. No claim about other Koszul lifts is made.

theorem tate_selfTor_conormal_map (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ c : conormalExteriorModule A I n ⟶
      ((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) n).obj (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I))).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I)), TateComparisonCertificate A I n c
